stories.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
stories.summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
stories.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's Darius Cooper.

The scoring picked up in the late window Sunday, as the Cowboys and Commanders combined for 57 points. However, Washington lost QB Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury in the second quarter -- hours after Chicago lost QB Caleb Williams to a right hamstring injury. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock.

The night game featured a wild ending, but ultimately the Kansas City Chiefs improved to 2-0 with an overtime thriller over the Indianapolis Colts.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

DET-BUF

Kansas City 33, Indianapolis 30 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Chiefs
Did Patrick Mahomes' performance demonstrate the Chiefs are back as contenders? That appears to be the case after two weeks. In overtime, Mahomes orchestrated the 25th winning drive of his 10-year career, which is tied with Kirk Cousins for second most in that span. Last season, the Chiefs were bad in one-score games, finishing with a 1-9 record. Mahomes, though, proved he's capable of carrying the Chiefs yet again to another dramatic win. In just his second game after recovering from the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, Mahomes finished with 382 passing yards and three touchdowns without committing a turnover.

Most surprising performance: Of course, Mahomes spent most of Sunday relying on tight end Travis Kelce, who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown. Yet receiver Tyquan Thornton was just as impactful for the Chiefs' offense. At pivotal moments, Thornton was impressive in catching all four of his targets for 86 yards, including a 45-yard reception. That highlight was the first time in the game that the Chiefs' offense converted on third down. -- Nate Taylor

Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Colts
Is this defense salvageable? The Colts' defense gave up its most yards in a game in three seasons in a Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens (506 yards). And the prospects for that unit didn't get better Sunday night, when the Colts consistently struggled to get stops against the Chiefs (523 yards). The question now is whether this is the permanent state of this defense, and if so, what does that mean for the 2026 Colts? Indianapolis approached this season knowing it needed a bit more from its defense to take some of the pressure of an offense led by QB Daniel Jones, who is coming off a torn Achilles tendon. But as of now, that plan is not panning out.

Most surprising performance: The Colts got a valiant effort from backup cornerback Kapena Gushiken, who came off the bench after injuries to starters Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner to make two clutch plays. One of them, a pass breakup on a third down late in the fourth quarter, was one of the biggest plays of the game. The stop against Rashee Rice ended the Chiefs' best last chance in regulation. -- Stephen Holder

Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Travis Kelce's 25.1 points were the second most among tight ends through the Sunday night game. Kelce caught nine of a team-high 11 targets, finishing with 101 yards and a touchdown. What stood out here? The play speed. We saw it with Kelce within the route and after the catch. Add that to his elite coverage awareness, too. It was a big night for Kelce, who is firmly in the TE1 ranks for the Week 3 game at Miami. -- Bowen

Dallas 37, Washington 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Cowboys
Are the Cowboys going to need QB Dak Prescott to outscore teams again this season? It looks that way. Prescott broke the Cowboys' record for touchdown passes in a career with four Sunday, eclipsing Tony Romo. But Prescott needed to be everything for Dallas, completing better than 80% of his passes, throwing the four scores and running for 26 yards. The defense had issues again, losing safety P.J. Locke (foot) and corner Cobie Durant (hamstring) in the first half. The Cowboys continue to struggle on third down, contain a running quarterback and turn pressures into sacks. Washington had three chances for touchdowns wiped out, but Prescott bailed the Cowboys out ... again.

Trend to watch: The Cowboys want to be a team that relies on the running game to get things going. Through two games, that has not happened. A week after running 18 times for 69 yards against the Giants, the Cowboys followed with 66 yards on 21 carries. No Cowboys running back has a rush of more than 9 yards. The Cowboys miss Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith, who will be out for at least the next two games because of thumb surgery, but they shouldn't miss him this much. -- Todd Archer

Next game: vs. Ravens (Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Commanders
What's next for Washington after QB Jayden Daniels' injury? This game resembled many from last season -- porous defense, an injured quarterback and a double-digit defeat. Daniels' status and length of absence remains uncertain. And he'll have to answer one giant question whenever he returns: Can he stay healthy? He has now exited four of his past five games with an injury. Also, the defense has struggled. In two games, it has forced zero turnovers and hasn't lived up to internal expectations. If the team is not careful, the season could get ugly.

Trend to watch: The Commanders' pass defense has allowed seven touchdown receptions in the first two games -- including four Sunday. The offseason overhaul on defense was supposed to help the coverage with intense pressure and disguised coverages. However, the pressure has been sporadic and too many targets are left open -- whether from coverage confusion or botched assignments. Cornerback Mike Sainristil has been a frequent target, and he's not the only one breaking down. -- John Keim

Next game: vs. Seahawks (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson had 20.3 fantasy points in Week 2, catching all four of his targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns. He will remain a touchdown-dependent player in this offense, but he is a priority target in scoring position. Ferguson already has three red zone targets over his first two games after seeing 23 last season. -- Bowen

Las Vegas 26, L.A. Chargers 14
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Raiders
How have the Raiders fared without TE Brock Bowers? Last year, the Raiders' offense fell apart when Bowers sustained a knee injury in Week 1. This year has been different. Las Vegas has been without Bowers (knee) for two weeks and has managed to make things work, which is a testament to coach Klint Kubiak. On Sunday, wide receiver Tre Tucker caught five passes for 119 yards and a touchdown. Las Vegas had eight players record a reception, including wide receiver Cody White, who had two touchdown catches. With Bowers expected to return for Week 3, the optimism for this offense grows higher.

What to make of the QB performance: After Kirk Cousins raised concerns about his ability to generate explosive passing plays, he let the ball fly at SoFi. On attempts of 10-plus air yards, Cousins completed 8 of 12 passes for 181 yards, three touchdowns and an interception. He had two completions for more than 40 yards each, including a 40-yard touchdown pass to Tucker. Cousins might not sling the ball like this every week, but at least he showed that he's still capable. -- Ryan McFadden

Next game: at Saints (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Chargers
What's up with the Chargers' passing offense? Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel was confident this week that his offense's Week 1 performance was an anomaly. Instead, the Chargers' offense was even more disjointed. Herbert didn't complete a pass of more than 20 air yards, as he was under constant pressure and receivers struggled to get open. He finished with 192 passing yards, one touchdown and an interception. There were also struggles from left tackle Joe Alt, who had three false-start penalties and a hold that resulted in a safety.

Trend to watch: Omarion Hampton had a career-high 23 carries for 92 yards and a touchdown. It was the first clear indication that the Chargers will lean on him this season. McDaniel has said previously that he would split the workload between the three backs: Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. But through the first two games, it has been clear that this is Hampton's backfield. -- Kris Rhim

Next game: at Bills (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Herbert disappointed yet again, throwing multiple interceptions for only the fifth time since the beginning of 2022. He seems out of sync with McDaniel's offense thus far, and he has a tough upcoming schedule (at the Bills, at Seahawks and at Broncos). It's best to look elsewhere for a QB streamer. -- Cockcroft

Seattle 31, Arizona 7
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Seahawks
Will Drew Lock have the Seahawks unbeaten by the time Sam Darnold returns? For the second straight week, the Seahawks showed they have the dominant defense, offensive weaponry and good enough backup quarterback to survive a stretch without their starter. Lock was 19-of-26 for 235 yards, three TDs and no turnovers. The Seahawks hope Darnold can practice this week, which suggests he might not have to miss more than another game or two. Seattle plays at Washington -- which lost Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury Sunday -- before hosting the 0-2 Chargers in Week 4.

Key stat to know: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year, finished with nine catches for 155 yards and has 11 games with at least 100 receiving yards since the start of last season. Per ESPN Research, that's the most in the NFL. Smith-Njigba also became the third Seahawk with 150-plus receiving yards and three receiving TDs in a game, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent (twice).

Best quote from the locker room: "We've been having a special connection for a minute now, but I'm super happy [for] the way he just came in and carried himself and carried this team. He shows time and time again how good he is," Jaxon Smith-Njigba said on his chemistry with Drew Lock. -- Brady Henderson

Next game: at Commanders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Cardinals
What went wrong for the defense in the second half? Arizona's defense went from stopping the run on a regular basis in the first half to hardly containing it in the second. Arizona gave up 43 rushing yards in the first two quarters, stopping the Seahawks twice within 4 yards of the end zone in the second quarter -- including on fourth-and-1 from the 1. But whatever worked in the first half didn't in the second, as Arizona allowed 109 yards in the final two quarters.

Key stat to know: The Cardinals gained 127 yards, which marked the first time they were held under 200 yards since November 2023, per ESPN Research. Arizona couldn't get anything going consistently offensively, with quarterback Jacoby Brissett throwing for 95 yards a week after passing for 277. -- Josh Weinfuss

Next game: at 49ers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Marvin Harrison Jr. isn't getting enough looks from Brissett, as he has run 58 routes and seen only four targets through two games. Five Cardinals have had more targets, including the clear "WR1" Trey McBride (who has 42.6 fantasy points this season). It's time to cut MHJ in fantasy. -- Cockcroft

San Francisco 35, Miami 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

49ers
Where do the 49ers go from here at wide receiver? The injury bug bit the Niners' wide receiver room again as Demarcus Robinson left on a cart with a right ankle injury. Though the Niners had no issues producing against the Dolphins without Robinson, the team's depth is growing perilously thin. Robinson joins Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling and Christian Kirk as injured 49ers wideouts. Making matters worse, Mike Evans had a hip issue late in the game but coach Kyle Shanahan said the WR would have returned if the game were closer. Kirk is eligible to return after Week 5, and with Robinson suffering a high ankle sprain, the Niners might need to scour the trade or free agent market for reinforcements.

Trend to watch: Beyond injuries, the 49ers' run defense continues to be their biggest issue. San Francisco limited the Dolphins to 3.5 yards per carry for the game, but Miami kept it close for a half because it controlled the ball and the clock. The Niners had just two first-half possessions, as the Dolphins mustered 60 rushing yards before first contact.

Best quote from the locker room: "Coming into this game, we knew the Dolphins, their whole story, it is what it is," QB Brock Purdy said about the Niners coming off a long trip to Australia and making sure they didn't have a letdown against a rebuilding opponent. "It's the NFL, you never know. Anything can happen on Sundays. And so for us, it's like how can we just be our best, play our way of football, and keep our heads down and let the game play out. That's what we were saying all week, and I thought we went out there and did that today."-- Nick Wagoner

Next game: vs. Cardinals (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Dolphins
Is there a bright spot for the Dolphins' defense moving forward? After this game, you'd be hard-pressed to find one. Jacob Rodriguez -- last week's standout -- was active Sunday, but it didn't make much of a difference as the 49ers' offense scored touchdowns on the team's first five drives. Without edge rusher Chop Robinson, the Dolphins' defense failed to generate pressure on Brock Purdy, and Miami couldn't affect him when he was forced out of the pocket. Life doesn't get much easier next week against Patrick Mahomes.

Trend to watch: Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis was pressured a whopping 17 times in Week 1, taking five sacks; and the heat stayed on him against the 49ers. Willis withstood 11 pressures and was brought down four times. Considering this is Miami's offensive line at full strength, the past two games have birthed a concerning trend. -- Marcel Louis-Jacques

Next game: vs. Chiefs (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Purdy has back-to-back games with at least 20 fantasy points, and he's doing an excellent job spreading the ball around. After Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr. starred in Week 1, it was George Kittle's turn. Purdy is a sneaky back-end fantasy QB1, and he's a great partner QB if you need help with that position. -- Cockcroft

Denver 20, Jacksonville 13
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Broncos
What is going on in the red zone for the Broncos' offense, especially in first-and-goal? The Broncos got just enough offense with just enough time left to win, but they continue to flirt with trouble in the red zone. The Broncos have scored just once on four first-and goal situations this season, and it came via rookie running Jonah Coleman on Sunday. Quarterback Bo Nix threw his second interception of the season in first-and-goal, and the Broncos have gone backward on two of those four drives. Toss in a 6-of-22 performance on third down this season, and the Broncos are not getting the situational work done that playoff teams do.

Trend to watch: Cancel the red alert on Jaylen Waddle's participation. He looked exactly like the player the Broncos made their biggest offseason move to acquire. After a one-catch, 2-yard evening against the Chiefs, Waddle had a team high in targets (10), catches (eight) and yards (138). Coach Sean Payton had promised Waddle would "get his touches," and he did just that in Week 2.

Best quote from the locker room: "Me, [Talanoa Hufanga], Justin [Strnad], Brandon [Jones], Riley [Moss], and Pat [Surtain II] and Ja'Quan [McMillian] all watched [last week's game] on the bus. Before the buses left Kansas City, left the parking lots, we had watched it, we knew what we had to do and [defensive coordinator Vance Joseph] knew that. [Last Monday] was embarrassing ... it was bring these guys together and play our brand of football. That's what we did," Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton on bouncing back from opening-week loss to the Chiefs. -- Jeff Legwold

Next game: vs. Rams (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Jaguars
Where was the Jaguars' pass rush? After five sacks against Cleveland, the Jaguars didn't sack Nix, and they hit him only three times. The Jaguars didn't really address their pass rush in the offseason, counting on the development of second-year players B.J. Green and Danny Striggow. They also banked on better coverage in the secondary -- led by the return of Travis Hunter -- making a difference. With Drake Maye, Joe Burrow, Jalen Hurts and C.J. Stroud on deck, Jacksonville's pass rush must be more consistent.

What to make of the QB performance: Trevor Lawrence got battered by the Broncos' pass rush, but unlike last season's matchup, the Jaguars weren't able to overcome it. Lawrence did make a few throws downfield -- the longest being a 32-yarder to Parker Washington to the 1-yard line -- when he did get good protection, but he had to rush a lot of throws. After his lone interception late in the third quarter, the Jaguars managed just 34 yards on three possessions.

Best quote from the locker room: "It comes down to all three phases in the second half, specifically fourth quarter, we did not win," coach Liam Coen said. "We didn't win it, we didn't coach it good enough, we didn't play good enough, and we did not finish. ... I thought we played complementary enough in the first half and that was what was disappointing was the complementary football, specifically in the second half. And as we went to the fourth quarter, when you needed a drive, you needed a stop, you needed a catch, you needed a play, we just didn't do it. We just didn't make it." -- Mike DiRocco

Next game: vs. Patriots (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Waddle scored 21.8 fantasy points in Week 2. With his catch-and-run ability, plus the vertical stretch speed, Waddle has the traits to mesh with the throwing style of Nix. Managers should keep Waddle in the WR2 range for Week 3. -- Bowen

Cleveland 23, Tampa Bay 19
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Browns
What did Deshaun Watson do to earn another start? With rumblings that his starting job was on the line, Watson delivered arguably his best game in a Browns uniform. His performance was risk-averse, as Watson's 3.7 air yards per attempt were his fewest in a game as a Brown. But he made big plays in the second half, converting four third-down conversions on a go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter. It was the type of outing that Cleveland has been waiting for years to see.

Key stat to know: The Browns had scored fewer than 20 points in eight straight Watson starts entering Sunday's matchup. This was Cleveland's first time cracking 20-plus points in a Watson start since Week 10 of the 2023 season, a 33-31 win over the Ravens.

Best quote from the locker room: "Browns are gonna Browns. F--- that!," said coach Todd Monken in response to Mike Tomlin's comments on Cleveland's Week 1 performance. -- Daniel Oyefusi

Next game: vs. Panthers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Buccaneers
Why have Baker Mayfield and the offense looked so out of sync? Mayfield just has not looked comfortable. The Bucs only found the end zone once -- in the third quarter with a 5-yard touchdown grab from Emeka Egbuka. The pair couldn't replicate this on fourth down with the game on the line after a lengthy weather delay. Mayfield also struggled to connect with Ted Hurst III (2-of-7 total and 1-of-4 on third down), including a 13-yard pass to the end zone he just couldn't hang onto in that final series. With the exception of a 49-yard dime to Tez Johnson, Mayfield struggled on the deep ball, where Mike Evans was always his most dependable weapon. He threw a first-quarter interception for his fourth turnover in two games.

Most surprising performance: No one has expected perfection, especially from a new piece navigating a new defense, but veteran linebacker Alex Anzalone has now surrendered eight receptions for 93 yards on eight targets -- along with a handful of missed tackles. That's not counting the plays in which he was out of position. The team signed him to not only bolster their coverage in the middle of the field, but they also believed in him enough to vote him a team captain. -- Jenna Laine

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Denzel Boston has big play juice and should be a priority waiver pickup this week. Rostered in only 26.4% of ESPN leagues, he scored 20.5 points, catching 5 of 7 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown. Boston has now posted a touchdown reception and at least 13 points in back-to-back games to start his pro career. -- Bowen

Philadelphia 24, Tennessee 20
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Eagles
How should we feel about the Eagles after this game? The offensive line was too leaky for the second straight week. The defense had issues suppressing an offense that ranked 31st in total yards (195) in Week 1. And quarterback Jalen Hurts, operating without running back Saquon Barkley (stinger) and tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) for much of the game, had two interceptions. Hurts orchestrated a touchdown drive in the final seconds to walk away with a win, but Philly's schedule is only going to get tougher from here.

What to make of the QB performance: Hurts threw an interception on the Eagles' opening drive -- his first on a pass thrown into the end zone since Week 10 of 2024 -- and another in the second half. But he bounced back to calmly lead the Eagles downfield in the closing moments before finding Darius Cooper for the game winner with 14 seconds left. -- Tim McManus

Next game: at Bears (Monday, Sept. 28, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Titans
What does this loss do for the Titans' confidence going forward? On paper, this game was lopsided. But both units fed off each other. Offensive coordinator Brian Daboll found a nice groove orchestrating two long scoring drives. The defense had interceptions by Amani Hooker and Marcus Harris that led to 10 points. But this is the kind of game the Titans need to find a way to win. Playing the Eagles closely could give them confidence going forward, but when will these turn into wins?

What to make of the QB performance: Ward appeared comfortable executing Daboll's offense. Both of the Titans' touchdowns came via Ward's legs, making him the fifth quarterback in franchise history with two rushing TDs in a game over the past 50 seasons. And Ward's 41-yard pass to Elic Ayomanor was the fourth longest of his career. -- Turron Davenport

Next game: at Giants (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Philly's DeVonta Smith showed genuine WR1 potential with 27.7 fantasy points, backed by a 38% target share. He is in prime position to shine with A.J. Brown now in New England, and Smith gets a fantastic matchup to repeat his Week 2 effort against the Bears. -- Cockcroft

Green Bay 20, N.Y. Jets 17 (OT)
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Packers
How badly did the Packers need this win? It wasn't just that their last win came 287 days ago. It wasn't just that they had lost six straight games, their longest losing streak since 1990-91. And it wasn't just that they would have been 0-2 for the first time since 2006, the longest active streak without an 0-2 start. Instead of blowing another late lead, they showed some grit and pulled off a 20-17 comeback win despite trailing 17-7 in the fourth quarter. It's the kind of victory that could boost the vibe around this team. Of course, that is unless potentially serious injuries to WR Jayden Reed (neck) and RT Zach Bako-Bewele take something away from this win.

Key stat to know: With 14 penalties (for 133 yards) against the Jets, the Packers have been called for 26 accepted penalties through two games. Previously, the most accepted penalties against the Packers in their first two games was 22 in 1947, according to ESPN Research. The 26 accepted penalties is tied for the fourth most by any team through its first two games in the Super Bowl era (since 1966). -- Rob Demovsky

Next game: vs. Falcons (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Jets
Are the Jets back to being the "Same Old Jets"? Coach Aaron Glenn is trying to change the losing culture, but it's hard to accomplish that when you blow a 10-point lead in the home opener, squandering a chance to go 2-0 for the first time since 2015. The Jets needed one timely play to secure the win, but they melted down in crunch time. Basically, they did everything possible to lose. Curiously, the Jets took the ball first in OT -- which, of course, backfired. This would've been a statement win, but it wound up the most crushing loss of the Glenn era.

Most surprising performance: The Jets' running game, so effective in Week 1, disappeared. Breece Hall (16 carries for 29 yards) was a nonfactor, putting a lot of strain on the passing attack. The most surprising part? Offensive coordinator Frank Reich was too pass-heavy throughout the game, taking the Jets out of their comfort zone. -- Rich Cimini

Next game: at Lions (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: The Packers used a committee approach for the second straight game. However, MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks combined for only 63 rushing yards. Sure, Lloyd caught a touchdown, but I wouldn't put much stock into that play. At this point, Green Bay's running backs provide very limited fantasy value. -- Bowen

Cincinnati 20, Houston 6
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Bengals
Is this the best start of the Zac Taylor era? Unequivocally, yes. For the second straight season, the Bengals start off 2-0. This time, quarterback Joe Burrow is healthy, and that is despite getting sacked five times Sunday. All of Cincinnati's stars played like stars, and that recipe can take the Bengals a long way. Perhaps the most noticeable change this season is the defense, which pressured QB C.J. Stroud all day and sacked him four times.

What to make of the QB performance: Given that he was sacked five times, that is one of Burrow's best outings. After dealing with a back issue earlier in the week, he finished 20-of-31 for 207 yards and two touchdowns -- both to Ja'Marr Chase -- without an interception. -- Ben Baby

Next game: at Steelers (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Texans
Can Houston survive without wideout Nico Collins? The Texans' offense struggled without Collins, who had a 7-75-1 line in the season opener against Buffalo but missed Sunday's game after a midweek hamstring injury. The wideout group of Jared Wayne, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel and Kayshon Boutte struggled, but tight end Dalton Schultz had 12 catches for 140 yards. Stroud went 30-of-55 for 353 yards. Luckily for the Texans, Collins' injury didn't appear to be serious.

Trend to watch: Houston's running backs have struggled with efficiency, but its offensive line hasn't given the push needed to create holes. Against the Bengals, David Montgomery and Woody Marks had 14 carries for 18 yards. In Week 1, the duo averaged 3.5 yards a carry. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Next game: at Colts (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: After a slow Week 1 start (3.2 fantasy points), Ja'Marr Chase bounced back with 26.5 fantasy points vs. one of the league's best defenses. Chase caught 7 of 9 targets for 75 yards, and he added two touchdowns. It's another reminder to trust your top picks in fantasy lineups. -- Bowen

Minnesota 9, Chicago 3
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Vikings
Could the defense have played any better? Honestly, no. The Bears' offense scored 56 fewer points than it did in Week 1. It's hard to make the point better than that. The Vikings held the Bears' rushing game largely in check, as D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai combined for 92 yards on 26 carries. And their pass defense bottled up quarterback Caleb Williams before his hamstring injury. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores blitzed him on 77% of his dropbacks, and Williams felt compelled to check down and throw short throughout the game.

Trend to watch: Playing with backup quarterback Carson Wentz, and with Week 1 leading rusher Jordan Mason on injured reserve, the Vikings leaned heavily on veteran running back Aaron Jones Sr. His 105-yard performance was his first 100-yard game since 2024, also against the Bears. -- Kevin Seifert

Next game: at Buccaneers (Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET)

Bears
Can the Bears' offense survive without Caleb Williams? Williams exited midway through the fourth quarter with a right hamstring injury sustained while trying to run in a touchdown. The Bears failed to score in his absence after struggling heavily with Flores' blitzes. And even with Williams, the offense did not resemble the one that put up 59 points last week. Chicago believes in backup quarterback Tyson Bagent and its ground game, which was the only way it generated momentum Sunday.

Most surprising performance: The same offensive line that paved the way for 291 rushing yards last week was out of sync from the start. Center Garrett Bradbury was flagged for four penalties, while left tackle Braxton Jones went in and out of the lineup, which Ben Johnson later said was by design. Bagent was sacked on the final play of the game after tight end Colston Loveland was left one-one-one with Vikings outside linebacker Dallas Turner. -- Courtney Cronin

Next game: vs. Eagles (Monday, Sept. 28, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Williams produced only 7.72 fantasy points before his injury. He rushed for 42 yards but managed just 138 passing yards and threw an interception. If Williams is out for an extended period, it will have major fantasy implications on Chicago's offense. -- Bowen

New Orleans 24, Baltimore 17
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Saints
How will the Saints fix their slow starts? The Saints put themselves into an early hole for the second week in a row, but it worked out this time with some second-half heroics. The slow starts on offense are becoming a pattern under coach Kellen Moore. According to ESPN Research, this is the Saints' fourth straight game without putting up points in the first quarter. It's their second-longest streak in the past 10 seasons and the longest since they went five straight games in 2021.

Trend to watch: According to ESPN Research, the Saints were 5-of-8 on third-and-long conversions (at least 7 yards) before scoring the go-ahead touchdown at the end of the game. The Saints might start slow, but they've already shown an ability in the past few weeks to make key conversions, particularly between Tyler Shough, Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. -- Katherine Terrell

Best quote from the locker room: Olave on whether this is one of the best wins he's ever had: "I feel like since I've been here, we haven't really beat a good team. I feel like it's been tough for us to be able to battle against good teams or great teams that make the playoffs every year. Baltimore, like I said, is a contender in the AFC. So just be able to battle, be able to show our resilience, be able to come in here and get a W was huge for us and we got to carry it over to next week." -- Katherine Terrell

Next game: vs. Raiders (Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Ravens
Why do the Ravens continue to lose leads in the fourth quarter? Baltimore thought it would change its fortune late in games by changing head coaches. But just like it did so many times under John Harbaugh, the Ravens failed to finish in the fourth quarter in Jesse Minter's second game. In Harbaugh's last five seasons with Baltimore, the Ravens lost an NFL-worst 14 games when leading through three quarters. Baltimore gave up two touchdown drives after entering the fourth quarter with a 17-9 lead Sunday. It will be debated whether Shough crossed the goal line on fourth-and-goal, but the Ravens had their chances to win. Quarterback Lamar Jackson's interception with 13 seconds left ended the game.

Trend to watch: With No. 1 target Zay Flowers out with a hamstring injury, Rashod Bateman stepped up to break out of a rut. He finished with seven catches for 88 yards, the fourth most of his career. This ended a streak of seven straight games of less than 50 yards receiving. Bateman also made a leaping 22-yard grab in the end zone, marking his first touchdown since Oct. 30, 2025. -- Jamison Hensley

Next game: vs. Cowboys (Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 4:25 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Saints RB Travis Etienne Jr. might struggle to approach last season's 296 touches. A week after losing goal-line carries to Kendre Miller, Etienne was out-carried and out-touched by Alvin Kamara, while Tyler Shough handled the game-winning TD sneak. Consider Etienne a low-end RB2. -- Cockcroft

Carolina 34, Atlanta 3
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Panthers
Will the real Panthers defense please stand up? One week after giving up 59 points and 552 yards to the Bears, Carolina's defense suffocated the Cooper Rush-led Atlanta offense. In the first half, the Panthers' defenders produced two turnovers and limited RB Bijan Robinson to 47 rushing yards. The takeaways were key, as Atlanta still picked up 162 net yards before halftime. On his first defensive play in the NFL, 2026 fifth-round pick Zakee Wheatley forced a fumble on Rush. Later, LB Devin Lloyd deflected a pass that was intercepted by Bobby Okereke. Lloyd, in particular, was revelatory with nine tackles (two for loss), a sack, three pass breakups, two third-quarter interceptions and a defensive touchdown.

What to make of the QB performance: Bryce Young looked the part of a franchise QB on Sunday. He threw for 204 yards and two touchdowns before halftime, spreading the ball around to Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker, Xavier Legette and Darren Waller. Playing point guard against a porous defense, Young continued his Mercedes-Benz Stadium dominance in the Panthers' third consecutive win in Atlanta. -- Mike Kaye

Next game: at Browns (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Falcons
Will the Falcons get some relief at quarterback in Week 3? Cooper Rush lost a fumble and threw an interception on the Falcons' first two drives. It was the first time the Falcons had two turnovers on back-to-back series to begin a game since 2007. Rush was later pulled for undrafted rookie Jack Strand, who threw a pick-six on his first attempt. ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Michael Penix Jr. could start in Week 3, but it wouldn't be ideal.

Key stat to know: Bijan Robinson surpassed 4,000 career rushing yards Sunday (72 yards) and is now tied for the second-fastest player to reach that mark (53 games) in NFL history, behind only Colts RB Jonathan Taylor. Robinson is tied with Josh Jacobs. Robinson is also now the fastest Falcons player to reach that total. -- Marc Raimondi

Next game: at Packers (Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Bryce Young scored 20-plus fantasy points in back-to-back games for the first time in his career, making great use of his deep set of receivers. We're used to him showing signs late in the season, but his hot start now elevates him into the solid-streaming tier for fantasy. -- Cockcroft

New England 20, Pittsburgh 3
Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Patriots
Are QB Drake Maye's lingering issues fixable? Maye's shaky decision-making and inaccuracy from the season opener carried over Sunday with a badly underthrown third-quarter interception. All four of Maye's interceptions this season have come on throws of 15-plus yards. He had four of those INTs all of last season. Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has preached patience and repetition with the 24-year-old Maye, who has faced two of the NFL's better defenses to open the season (Seahawks and Steelers) and now looks ahead to road games against the Jaguars and Bills.

Key stat to know: Running back TreVeyon Henderson's 39-yard touchdown rush in the first quarter was his fifth one of 30-plus yards since the start of last season, which leads the NFL. Henderson missed the season opener with an ankle injury, and coach Mike Vrabel said the team would welcome his ability to create explosive plays, which showed up quickly Sunday.

Best quote from the locker room: "Just trying to win the game. You're not gonna ruin my Sunday," said coach Mike Vrabel when asked about the concern he has for the offense. -- Mike Reiss

Next game: at Jaguars (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Steelers
Is it time to make a change on the offensive line? The O-line failed to protect 42-year-old QB Aaron Rodgers or get push in the run game. Rodgers was sacked four times, including a strip sack returned for a game-sealing touchdown after Spencer Anderson was manhandled by Christian Barmore. Under pressure, Rodgers was 4-of-11 for 18 yards, with two sacks and two fumbles. The run game averaged 4.0 yards per carry a week after averaging 2.8. The Steelers could turn to veteran Brock Hoffman to replace Anderson at right guard, and they could replace tackle Dylan Cook with rookie Max Iheanachor if they wanted to.

Trend to watch: DK Metcalf picked up where he left off in Week 1 -- and not in a good way. He had four catches on nine targets for 27 yards, with at least two drops. Metcalf has eight catches on 19 targets for 67 yards this season. For most of the day, he struggled to get separation from top Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez. Metcalf added a pair of catches in the fourth quarter, but it was too little, too late.

Best quote from the locker room: "Offense needs to be better. Mike McCarthy needs to be better," said coach Mike McCarthy after the Steelers' offensive struggles in the loss. -- Brooke Pryor

Next game: vs. Bengals (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Fantasy football takeaway: Maye is already halfway (four) to his entire 2025 interception total (eight). Repeating last season's stellar accuracy metrics was an unrealistic ask, but this much regression raises red flags ... especially with one of the league's toughest schedules in 2026. If you roster Maye, a start-worthy bench QB is now mandatory. -- Cockcroft

stories.headline: The clause that may save Lions ace for Grand Final
stories.summary: The Brisbane Lions are set to use a fresh clause when trying to save dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale from being suspended for the AFL Grand Final.
stories.body:
The AFL tribunal chairman was blunt: the 'good bloke' clause doesn't exist.

Instead, tribunal chair Jeff Gleeson KC turned to a fresh provision in the AFL's laws, centred on compelling and exceptional circumstances.

It's the clause that could save Brisbane's Lachie Neale from being suspended for Saturday's Grand Final.

The Lions will challenge Neale's one-game suspension for striking Hawthorn's Jack Ginnivan in last Saturday night's Preliminary Final.

Neale's gut punch on Ginnivan was graded intentional conduct, medium impact and body contact.

On video evidence, Neale is guilty.

"There's no point putting energy into it until we know the result," Neale's teammate Jarrod Berry told reporters on Monday.

"We'll be sitting tight and praying that he gets off. But if he doesn't, we'll face it when it comes."

Precedents this season have resulted in one-game bans to numerous players - the most recent just last week, when Adelaide's Max Michalanney was suspended for delivering an off-the-ball gut punch.

But what may allow Neale, a dual Brownlow medallist to play in the premiership decider is the clause that saved Collingwood legend Scott Pendlebury from suspension in March.

'Exceptional and compelling circumstances' is certain to be the anchor of Brisbane's argument at Tuesday night's tribunal hearing.

The Lions will cite Pendlebury's hearing on March 17 this year.

The acts in the cases of Pendlebury and Neale are starkly different.

The Magpie great was charged with rough conduct for a bump on Adelaide's Josh Worrell.

His proposed one-match suspension was downgraded to a $3000 fine with Gleeson enacting the 'compelling and exceptional circumstances' clause.

Pendlebury's advocate Myles Tehan successfully argued the ex-Pies captain "stands in a class of his own", having never previously been before the tribunal in a 21-year AFL career.

"It's frankly difficult to imagine how it could not constitute an exceptional and compelling circumstance (to avoid a ban)," Tehan told the hearing.

"I should say this is not by any means a good bloke clause or a get of jail free card or anything of that nature."

Tribunal chair Gleeson then interjected.

"I might add, it never has been. It's misreported as being something to that effect from time to time," Gleeson said.

"But people who read the guidelines and listen to what the tribunal says will understand it's nothing to do with being a good bloke.

"It's to do with whether the circumstances are exceptional and compelling."

The relevant clause states: "Players will not automatically receive a reduced sanction for a good record. However, if a classifiable offence is contested or referred to the tribunal, a player with an exemplary record may argue that their good record constitutes exceptional and compelling circumstances".

Neale, a 320-gamer, is a dual Brownlow medallist; a dual premiership captain; a four-time All Australian; a four-time club champion who, like Pendlebury, has never been suspended.

His exemplary history gives the Lions cause to argue - and hope for a reprieve.

stories.headline: Dreyer outduels Messi as San Diego hands Miami 4th straight draw
stories.summary: Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi scored his 101st goal for Inter Miami CF, but Anders Dreyer scored twice for San Diego FC, as the teams played to a 2-2 draw on Sunday night.

It was Inter Miami's fourth consecutive draw in MLS play as new manager Kily González oversaw his first league game in charge of the club and cut a frustrated figure after conceding a late goal to drop points.

"We've been here for four days and haven't been able to train properly. Defensively, we really need to be much stronger," González said after the game. "We can't commit these defensive horrors, they come at a high cost. That final situation shouldn't have happened. It's surreal to be in a position to win the game, yet nearly lose it.

"We only avoided defeat because our goalkeeper saved us."

Dreyer gave San Diego a 1-0 lead in the 12th minute, capitalizing on a through ball from Jeppe Tverskov before deftly chipping over goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Messi answered in the 24th with his 20th league goal of the season. His free kick from the right side went untouched through the penalty area and into the far side of the net, four days after he scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami in a 2-0 win over Mexican side Cruz Azul in the Campeones Cup.

"I think the Campeones Cup might have had an unconscious effect, especially in the first half, leading to a bit of complacency," González added. "These are factors that are part of football. At a club where we are obliged to win every match we play, we have to rise to the occasion. We made significant adjustments at halftime to get the team flowing and ensure we stayed compact, keeping the lines tight so we wouldn't suffer the way we did in the first half."

The goal was Messi's eighth from a free kick since entering the league in 2023, more than any other player in MLS during that time span.

Luis Suárez put Miami ahead in the 74th minute as Miami looked set to leapfrog New England into second place in the Eastern Conference, but Dreyer scored his second of the night eight minutes later with another fine finish -- this time from a ball over the top of the Herons' backline.

Miami is now in third place with a record of 12-4-10 with 46 points -- 11 behind first-place Nashville.

"But anyway, we have to keep going," González said. "On the positive side, we did some good things, but I need to fine-tune the defensive side because that's what really worries me most."

Earlier Sunday, FIFA announced that the final phase of the 2027 FIFA Women's Champions Cup will be played at Inter Miami's home of Nu Stadium in January. FIFA Chief Football Officer Jill Ellis spoke at halftime about bringing the competition to Miami.

"I think we've seen that this city loves its football. We've seen it this past summer with the World Cup," Ellis said. "I think it's time to bring a major women's tournament here to Miami. I think it's exciting."

Miami returns to MLS play next Sunday on the road against the Columbus Crew, while San Diego is also on the road with a game against Austin FC on Saturday.

ESPN writer Lizzy Becherano contributed to this report, while information from The Associated Press was also used.

stories.headline: Raptors honor Kyle Lowry with golden 'GROAT' statue
stories.summary: Lowry also received a key to the city of Toronto and a special dinner to honor his contribution to the franchise.
stories.body:
With a sea of red, white and black Kyle Lowry jerseys filling the streets of Toronto for an honorary block party, the guard's legacy will forever be stamped in the city's lore with an exclusive commemorative figure.

On Saturday, the Toronto Raptors honored Lowry's career with a block party outside of Scotiabank Arena, unveiling a golden raptor statue. The sculpture features Lowry's No. 7 jersey while dribbling a basketball and stands on a nameplate that reads "The Greatest Raptor of All Time. Kyle Lowry | 2012-2021, 2026."

The statue unveiling follows the franchise's August announcement that it would retire Lowry's jersey number during the upcoming 2026-27 season. It will be raised to the rafters at the conclusion of Toronto's home matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers on Jan. 10.

Along with the statue, the six-time All-Star received a key to the city.

"I've been looking forward to this moment for years. I always said that Toronto is home, and that I'd retire a Raptor, and to see my No. 7 go up in that building is going to mean everything to me," Lowry said. "We built something special here -- my teammates, the organization, the city and the fans, and all of Canada. We became champions together, and to be able to share this night with all of them, and with my family, is going to mean a lot to me."

Lowry, who spent nine of his 20 seasons in Toronto, helped bring the Raptors their only NBA championship in the 2019 NBA Finals. He will also join Basketball Hall of Famer Vince Carter as the only Raptors to have their numbers retired -- Carter's was retired in November 2024.

The 40-year-old Lowry announced his retirement in July after signing a one-day contract with Toronto to retire as a member of the franchise.

He averaged 13.8 points, 4.2 rebounds and six assists in his 20 seasons.

stories.headline: UFC 331 takeaways: Are we living in the greatest era for lightweights?
stories.summary: Arman Tsarukyan and Joshua Van stole the show with emphatic statements at UFC 331.
stories.body:
The main card of UFC 331 had shocking moments on top of shocking moments on top of pound-for-pound resume building.

First, Sean Sharaf got his first UFC win as the biggest underdog in the promotion's history against Olympic gold medalist Gable Steveson in just 12 seconds. Then Arman Tsarukyan stepped into the cage for the first time this year and reminded everyone why the current crop of UFC lightweights may be the best ever. And flyweight champion Joshua Van followed it all up with a performance that should place him among the 10 best MMA fighters in the world right now. What more could an MMA fan want?

Van is a top five pound-for-pound fighter
I can't believe I'm saying this -- not because Van isn't great or hasn't been great for some time. It's just -- how does one become a top-five fighter in the world at age 24, with less than five years of pro experience?

After his performance on Saturday, I can't talk about Van anymore as just a phenom or a young champion. He is legitimately as good as just about anyone in the entire sport. Alexandre Pantoja coming off injury looked like the same Pantoja as before the injury. If anything, he looked even more determined than before. His pressure was appropriate and his decision-making was sound. Van was just better.

He defended takedowns and escaped on the ground when Pantoja could get him there. At one point, was it just me or did Van catch Pantoja's glove as he threw a punch, before countering? He caught some of Pantoja's kicks, in the same way he caught the one in December that led to Pantoja's injury. In the fifth round, when the result of the fight still felt up in the air, Van delivered his best five minutes of work, dropping Pantoja with a right hand.

Van is gifted athletically, confident and a natural finisher. He's been all of that from the first moment we saw him. One description that shouldn't be forgotten, however, is that he's extremely technical. This was one of the most technical fights of the entire year, against one of the best flyweights of all time, and Van ended up running away on the scorecards. If Van were 28, I don't think anyone would have an issue ranking him near the top of the pound-for-pound. The only hesitancy to do it is because -- it doesn't seem right or possible, given his age and relative inexperience. I'm getting over that. Van is top five. -- Brett Okamoto

Are we living in the greatest lightweight era of all time?

The history of the UFC's lightweight division is so undeniably rich. One of the division's greatest "eras" was from 2016 to 2020, when Conor McGregor became double champ at Madison Square Garden, Khabib Nurmagomedov dominated and timeless fighters such as Tony Ferguson, Dustin Poirier and Justin Gaethje were in their primes.

This upcoming chapter at lightweight has a chance to challenge all that.

Within the past three months, Ilia Topuria has suffered his first loss (in spectacular fashion to Gaethje on the White House lawn) and vowed revenge. Paddy Pimblett has turned in a star-making performance, submitting Benoît Saint Denis in less than a minute on a McGregor-headlined card. And now Arman Tsarukyan has completed an unbelievable walkoff knockout of Mauricio Ruffy. Topuria, Pimblett and Tsarukyan are three legitimate superstar storylines, and it just so happens they are all rivals who have promised to take each other out.

Don't forget that the champion, Gaethje, could postpone retirement in order to defend his throne. Veterans Max Holloway and Charles Oliveira are still active in the top five, too. Australia's Quillan Salkilld has had a breakout year, and Nurmagomedov's younger cousin, Usman, could potentially transition to the UFC after years of dominance in the PFL.

Yeah. The next few years could be the best in lightweight history, and that is really, really saying something. -- Okamoto

The Steveson train has hit an early crossroads

It's not like Steveson had never lost before. On his way to becoming a 2020 Olympic wrestling gold medalist and two-time NCAA Division I national champion, he was formidable but not perfect. His record at the University of Minnesota was 103-3. His international freestyle record, including cadet and junior levels, was 53-2. Even an all-time great has had to pick himself up and dust himself off at times.

But this defeat was different from whatever Steveson had ever experienced. He got knocked out cold in 12 seconds by Sharaf, a guy who came into their fight 0-2 in the UFC with both losses coming by knockout. Let's just acknowledge that this matchmaking was a setup to build an MMA résumé for Steveson. Considering that he had just four pro fights under his belt, though, this was an appropriate booking.

The result was a shocker. It was the largest known upset in UFC history, per DraftKings. But what's done is done, and the story now takes an unexpected twist. Will this be just a speed bump on Steveson's express road toward the top of the UFC heavyweight division? Or will this defeat make Steveson timid in standup fighting, slowing his development beyond being a one-dimensional wrestler? Heavy-handed UFC heavyweights will surely be emboldened by seeing Steveson crash to the canvas. What seemed like a sure thing now is surrounded by question marks. The future might still be bright for Steveson. It probably will be. Here's a suggestion for Steveson: Don't bother watching the 12-second KO loss. Why put yourself through that again? Instead, go find video of Islam Makhachev's 2015 KO loss in his second UFC fight, then contemplate how Makhachev has managed to win all 17 of his fights since on his way to becoming the best pound-for-pound fighter in the sport. -- Jeff Wagenheim

stories.headline: Azerbaijan Grand Prix 2026: Race start time in Baku, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

stories.body:
Formula 1 is heading to the streets of Baku for this year's Azerbaijan Grand Prix as we roll into the business end of the season.

Title leader Kimi Antonelli extended his lead in the drivers' championship after picking up his eighth victory of the season at the brand-new Madring last time out.

He leads his teammate George Russell by 81 points, with Lewis Hamilton now dropping back in the title race after a retirement in Spain.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 15th race of the season.

- Madring's F1 debut left everyone dissatisfied, even Spanish GP's top 3

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters in 35 minutes

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Azerbaijan Grand Prix schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, September 24

Practice One: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Practice Two: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Friday, September 25

Final Practice: 9.30 a.m. - 10.30 a.m.

Qualifying: 1 p.m. - 2 p.m.

Saturday, September 26

Azerbaijan Grand Prix: 12 p.m.

How to watch

Sky Sports has exclusive F1 rights again in 2026 in the U.K., with every session live on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Why is the race on a Saturday?
For the first time in Baku's history, the F1 weekend will shift a day forwards, with the race taking place on a Saturday to avoid a clash with an Azerbaijan National Day of mourning on the Sunday.

Azerbaijan's people will dedicate their thoughts to military personnel and those who died during the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War.

Baku City Circuit

After the European leg of the calendar where circuits are more traditional, Baku is one of the standout street circuits of the season.

The first race in Baku was held in 2016 as the European Grand Prix before it was called the Azerbaijan Grand Prix a year later.

The section around Turns 8, 9 and 10 are lined by the walls of the city's charming old town including a castle and the long main straight along the Baku shoreline sees cars reach speeds in excess of 220 mph and is the best spot for overtaking.

The walls are narrow and the high-speeds make for either a race full of chaos, or none at all. There is a 57% chance of a Safety Car being deployed during the race.

Azerbaijan Grand Prix

Circuit: Baku City Circuit; Baku, Azerbaijan

Previous winners
2016: Nico Rosberg (Mercedes)

2017: Daniel Ricciardo (Red Bull)

2018: Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes)

2019: Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes)

2021: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2022: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

2023: Sergio Pérez (Red Bull)

2024: Oscar Piastri (McLaren)

2025: Max Verstappen (Red Bull)

Other key stats

First F1 race: 2016 European GP. (First race as Azerbaijan GP in 2017)

Laps: 51 laps of 6km.

Lap record: 1:43.009, Charles Leclerc (2019).

Most wins: Pérez (2021, 2023) and Verstappen (2022, 2025) with two wins each. Other winners from the current grid are Hamilton (2018), Bottas (2019) and Piastri (2024).

Most poles: Leclerc with four (2021-2024) and Hamilton (2017), Bottas (2019) and Verstappen (2025) are the other pole sitters from the current grid.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix will be dry and sunny throughout the weekend. Temperatures will be around 26°C, but will drop to 24°C for the race on Saturday.

What happened last year?
Red Bull's Verstappen took pole position around the streets of Baku in a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags.

He ended up converting that pole into a dominant victory, with Russell in second and Carlos Sainz behind.

It was a key moment in the championship fight between Lando Norris and Piastri as Norris closed the gap to 25 points to his McLaren teammate after the Australian crashed out.

Who will win this year?

The last street circuit this year was in Monaco in June and since then several of the top teams have upgraded its packages and haven't yet gone racing on street circuits, but Baku has now arrived.

Antonelli has looked on fire in the last two races, but Norris is creeping to the front. The reigning world champion has two wins to his name in Hungary and Zandvoort, but also suffered an unlucky run in Madrid with the safety car deployment, so missed out on a potential win there as well.

Mercedes are set to be quick in the high-speed straight lines in Baku, but the tight and twisty corners might suit Ferrari and McLaren best.

One of the main aims will be to not crash the car into the wall otherwise the whole course of the race can rapidly change in a blink of an eye.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL investigating after referee peppered with rubbish
stories.summary: Warriors great Shaun Johnson has labelled footage of fans throwing projectiles at referee Ashley Klein in Auckland as embarrassing, with the NRL investigating.
stories.body:
The NRL has been urged to come down hard on supporters who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles as the league's integrity unit investigates the ugly aftermath of Newcastle's semi-final win over the Warriors.

Vision from Eden Park after fulltime in the Knights' 12-10 victory showed Klein being hit with a raft of bottles, cups and rubbish as he walked from the field.

The footage shows Klein having to be protected by security, as fans abused the veteran referee and projectiles rained down on him.

The NRL immediately launched an investigation into potential breaches of their spectators' code of conduct. An Integrity Unit investigator had been at the ground.

"If found guilty, they will be banned for a period of time from attending NRL games," ARL Commission chairman Peter V'landys told AAP.

V'landys' no-nonsense stance was welcomed by the the referee's union, Professional Rugby League Match Officials (PRLMO), who called on the NRL to come down hard on the Warriors supporters.

"The safety of all referees and match officials is paramount, and they should be allowed to perform their duties without being placed in harm's way," PRLMO chair John Choueifate told AAP.

"To say I was disappointed is an understatement and call on the NRL to investigate the incident which detracted from an enthralling match.

"They need to send a very clear message to those responsible and to others in future that this rubbish must be stamped out of the game."

New Zealand Police have since confirmed that no arrests were made, with "no issues to note" other than two pitch invaders.

The Warriors did not respond to requests for comment.

Sunday's crowd of 48,511 marked the biggest ever for a rugby league match in New Zealand, after the NRL made the call to move the game from the Warriors traditional Mt Smart Stadium home.

The fan abuse came after two contentious calls went against the Warriors late in the match, including a decision not to penalise Tyson Frizell for an escort in the dying minutes.

Warriors great Shaun Johnson hit out at the fans' response after the match, labelling it "embarrassing".

"It leaves a bit of a sour taste in your mouth, what has been an unbelievable night with the colours, the energy, the happiness and celebration," Johnson said on Sky NZ's coverage.

"But there is just no need for it. It's just embarrassing.

"Ashley Klein has probably refereed the best game of rugby league I have seen in a long time tonight.

"He didn't take any gamesmanship in terms of people laying down. He didn't let people approach him whinging.

"He didn't make the game about him. He let the players come and play and they dictated the outcome."

Warriors coach Andrew Webster had vented his frustration in the post-match press conference, highlighting a bunker strip call on Te Maire Martin and the decision not to penalise Frizell for a possible escort on Leka Halasima.

The incident comes after AFL umpires also had cans thrown at them while leaving the MCG after Hawthorn's tight loss to Brisbane in Saturday night's preliminary final.

The AFL has also condemned the behaviour and warned of minimum five-year bans for any fans found responsible.

stories.headline: Dockers name club icon Shaun McManus as premiership cup presenter
stories.summary: Inaugural Fremantle player Shaun McManus will present the AFL premiership cup to captain Alex Pearce if the Dockers are successful on the grand final stage.
stories.body:
Fremantle pioneer Shaun McManus will hand over the AFL premiership cup to captain Alex Pearce if the Dockers break through for their maiden flag.

Part of the inaugural 1995 Dockers squad, McManus has been named as Fremantle's cup presenter ahead of Saturday's grand final against back-to-back reigning premiers Brisbane.

The Lions have yet to name their presenter after three-time premiership player Jonathan Brown did so for last year's decider win over Geelong.

McManus was given the nod amid speculation two-time Brownlow medallist Nat Fyfe, who retired last season, would do the honours.

Peter Bell was named the club's presenter for the eventual 2013 grand final loss to Hawthorn.

Dockers chief Simon Garlick described McManus as a perfect embodiment of the club's values.

McManus began his AFL career as a 19-year-old, going on to play 228 games across 14 seasons.

He captained the team alongside Adrian Feltcher from 2000 to 2001, and played alongside current coach Justin Longmuir.

"Shaun perfectly sums up what a Fremantle person is," Garlick said in a club statement.

"He had a remarkable career as a Fremantle player, but beyond that he has been a champion of this club since our humble beginnings back in 1995.

"Those early foundation years weren't easy, and as a 19-year-old he came in, showed great qualities which resulted in him being named captain at just 24.

"The courage he showed on field speaks for itself, but ever since retiring he's been a passionate and positive influence, someone who purely lives and breathes Freo.

"If we are good enough to get the job done on Saturday, it will be a great moment to see Shaun present the cup to Alex, and his old teammate Justin."

McManus is the ninth-highest game record holder in the club's history and was the second behind Shane Parker to reach the 200-game milestone.

Retiring after the 2008 season, McManus remained at the club as a player development coach and transitioned through various off-field roles.

The 50-year-old became a Dockers life member in 2004.
